provenance: Ex coll Emil Bader, Biel. Acquired by museum 1902.
literature: Waterhouse 1993: 177; Senn 1999 (including photocopies from Museum’s inventory cards).
remarks: Not a trombone, from the look of the photo in Senn 1999. It appears to be a valveless, slideless instrument with attached mp. It has three coils of tubing, the first being very small and apparently fitted with a tuning slide, or at least a brace at the distal end. The last coil terminates in a dragon’s-head bell with (apparently) a moveable tongue that oscillates when the instrument is blown. A small brace connects the second coil to the dragon-shead bell. Waterhouse 1993 lists it as a trombone. It is possible that at some point in its life—perhaps even originally—the instrument was fitted with a slide. In its present form it seems unfit for anything except bugle calls, though it is probably too low in pitch for this purpose. Inventory card supplied in Senn 1999 indicates that it is a bell from a trombone.
